tagline: Training-free refusal removal for LLMs, tuned automatically by Optuna

scenes.narration: Day 59: Heretic, an open-source tool that removes a model's refusal behavior with no retraining at all, tested on a CPU-only machine.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: Finds the direction that causes refusals
Optuna auto-tunes how strongly to remove it
scenes.narration: Heretic finds the direction inside a model's activations that triggers refusals, then lets Optuna tune how strongly to remove it.

steps.narration: ARA compares harmless and harmful prompts and extracts one residual-stream direction that corresponds to refusal.
Optuna searches how strongly and in which layers to remove that direction, every trial running on plain CPU.
Each trial is scored on refusal rate and KL divergence from the original model, and the best trade-off becomes the final model.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Refusal rate on 20 held-out harmful prompts, before and after. Selected trial's KL divergence: 0.0000.
scenes.narration: On Qwen3-0.6B, baseline refusal rate was 6 out of 20. After 12 Optuna trials, refusals dropped to zero, with a reported KL divergence of 0.0000, in twelve minutes on CPU.
Full numbers and reproduction steps are on Zenn and GitHub. Heretic is AGPL-3.0.
